01 / How I Think

Five principles I refuse
to stop believing.

Hover any card to see the reasoning behind the belief.

01

Don't give me the solution.

Give me the problem.

"Users want a faster search" is a feature request.
"Users give up before finding what they need" is a problem.
Only the second one leads somewhere worth building.

02

Challenge the obvious.

"Users asked for it" is not evidence.

Users describe symptoms. The PM diagnoses the disease.
If you build what users ask for, you're a feature factory.
If you build what they actually need, you're building a product.

03

Name the trade-off.

Speed vs quality. Growth vs retention. Accuracy vs latency.

The worst decisions are where nobody said "we are choosing X over Y."
In AI products: cost / latency / accuracy is the permanent triangle.
Name it. Own it. Revisit it when the context changes.

04

Ship something.

A perfect PRD that never ships is beautifully formatted fiction.

I'd rather own a shipped v1 with known limitations
than a polished v0.9 that never left Notion.
The product is the experiment. Ship it, measure it, iterate.

05

Measure reality.

If the metric didn't move, the idea didn't work.

Not "we shipped it." Not "users liked it in testing."
The metric. Did it move? By how much? Compared to what?
That's how we know. Then we go again.

PhonePe App
→

Friction Hand-off to partner NBFC's own flow breaks continuity and trust — a structural problem single-lender models don't have.
AI Fix Embedded partner flows within PhonePe's design shell + cross-partner context carry-over via AI agent at hand-off boundary.
Success Metric Hand-off completion rate (primary) · partner NPS post-loan-disbursement (secondary)

Reliability Framework for Quantized VLMs

Identified a real product risk: quantized AI models (cheaper to run) hallucinate more on edge hardware. Scoped and built an original technical solution.

PM Lens

This is the cost / latency / accuracy triangle that every AI PM navigates when deciding which model to ship. I built a framework for making that decision defensible — with a non-parametric drift detector and a cost-aware two-tier inference cascade.

Approach Non-parametric density-drift detector + GPU/CPU inference cascade with conformal prediction thresholds
Status Two rounds of external peer review completed · revision submitted to IEEE journal
Advised by Dr. K. E. Srinivasa Desikan

05 / Things I Believe

Product philosophy.
No fluff.

—

"The user asked for a feature" is not a problem statement.

—

More features ≠ better product. Fewer sharp ones, shipped well, do more.

—

Data should challenge my opinion, not decorate my presentation.

—

If I can't explain the product to a non-technical user, I probably don't understand it yet.

—

A PRD isn't sacred. The problem statement is.

—

In AI products: cost / latency / accuracy is a triangle, not a checklist. Pick two deliberately.

—

Hallucination isn't an engineering problem. It's a product risk that needs a mitigation strategy at the spec stage.

—

The metric that didn't move is the most important thing in the retrospective.
